question.problem:
The height (in feet) and the average number of points scored per game (APG) of four players on a basketball team are shown in the following table. 

| Height $(x)$ | **$6$** | **$6.5$** | **$6.5$** | **$7$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| APG $(y)$ | $5$ | $8$ | $10$ | $10$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the average number of points scored per game by a player whose height is $6.45\,\text{ft}?$

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}84.75 & -13 \\ -13 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}33 \\ 217\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
question.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 1 & 6.5 \\ 1 & 6.5 \\ 1 & 7\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 8 \\ 10 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

 

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =[\begin{aligned}84.75 & -13 \\ -13 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}33 \\ 217\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-24.25 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=-24.25+5x.$ 

Finally, to predict the average number of points scored per game by a player whose height is $6.45\,\text{ft},$  we substitute $x=6.45$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-24.25+5(6.45) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model,  the average number of points scored per game by a player whose height is $6.45\,\text{ft}$ will be $8$  points per game.
